title: Can ChatGPT Pass High School Exams on English Language Comprehension?
venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether ChatGPT can solve a real high-stakes reading comprehension exam at the high-school level, and whether performance differs across model versions and prompting strategies. The motivation is not to test an instructional intervention, but to benchmark the capability of large language models on an authentic educational assessment in English reading comprehension.

The study applied GPT-3.5 and two versions of GPT-4 (March 2023 and June 2023 updates) to Dutch national VWO English reading comprehension exams from 2022. The exams included multiple-choice and open-ended items, and the author compared model scores to official scoring standards and to student performance on one exam. GPT-3.5 performed around the average student level overall, while GPT-4 outperformed the average student, with the best performance coming from GPT-4-0314.

A secondary analysis used repeated API sampling to examine self-consistency across 50 runs per exam item. This showed that GPT-4 was usually consistent, but inconsistency often coincided with incorrect answers. The paper concludes that ChatGPT can generate valid answers to reading comprehension questions at scale, raising concerns about assessment integrity and suggesting that future educational assessment may need to adapt to AI availability. The strongest evidence in the paper is on multiple-choice reading comprehension items, where GPT-4 showed the clearest improvement over GPT-3.5; there is no direct comparison to instructional interventions such as teacher-led literacy instruction or tutoring.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's large language model chatbot system used to generate responses to user prompts and perform text-based question answering.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to answer Dutch national high school English reading comprehension exam questions, via the web interface for GPT-3.5 and via API for GPT-4; performance was compared across versions and against human student exam results.

findings.finding_summary: On Dutch national VWO English reading comprehension exams (2022), GPT-3.5 achieved an overall mean grade of 7.3 on the Dutch 1–10 scale (6.5 without re-prompting), compared with the average student grade of 6.99 on Exam 1. GPT-4-0314 and GPT-4-0613 scored higher, with overall mean grades of 8.3 and 8.1, respectively; no effect size was reported.
findings.measure: Exam score / converted grade on English reading comprehension national exams
findings.sample_size: n=124 questions across 3 exams; student comparison available for Exam 1 only (n=35,698 students)

quality_tier_rationale: This is a single benchmark-style assessment study rather than an RCT, quasi-experiment, or classroom intervention study. It provides useful descriptive evidence about reading comprehension performance, but not causal evidence about instructional impact.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported exam grades suggest substantial performance on reading comprehension items, especially for GPT-4, but this is an assessment benchmark rather than an educational intervention effect. No effect size is reported, so impact is difficult to quantify beyond the raw scores.
